mcqs.question: Which of the following statements gives the correct definition of a function from set A to set B?

options.A: A function assigns to each element of A exactly one element of B.
options.B: A function assigns to each element of B at most one element of A.
options.C: A function assigns to each element of A at least one element of B.
options.D: A function assigns to each element of A possibly many elements of B.

mcqs.answer: A function assigns to each element of A exactly one element of B.
mcqs.explanation: Option A correctly states that a function gives every input (element of the domain A) exactly one output in the codomain B. Option B reverses the roles of domain and codomain. Option C allows more than one output for an input, which violates the definition. Option D explicitly says an input may have many outputs, which is not allowed for a function.

mcqs.question: Consider the set of ordered pairs R = {(1,2), (1,3), (2,4)}. Which statement correctly distinguishes R as a relation and whether it is a function?

options.A: R is a relation but not a function because the element 1 in the domain is related to two different outputs.
options.B: R is a function because each element of the domain has exactly one output.
options.C: R is neither a relation nor a function.
options.D: R is a function only if we restrict the codomain to {2,3,4}.

mcqs.answer: R is a relation but not a function because the element 1 in the domain is related to two different outputs.
mcqs.explanation: Any set of ordered pairs is a relation, so R is certainly a relation. For a relation to be a function, each input must have exactly one output. Here the input 1 is paired with both 2 and 3, violating that rule, so R is not a function. Option B is false because of this duplication. Option C is false because R is a relation. Option D is irrelevant; changing the codomain does not affect the mapping rule that an input must have a single output.

mcqs.question: For the function f: {‑2,0,1} → {0,1,2,3} defined by f(‑2)=1, f(0)=0, f(1)=3, select the correct identification of domain, codomain, and range.
mcqs.explanation: The domain is the set of all inputs, which are {‑2,0,1}. The codomain is the set declared as the target set, {0,1,2,3}. The range (image) consists of the actual outputs produced: f(‑2)=1, f(0)=0, f(1)=3, giving {0,1,3}. Option B swaps domain and codomain. Option C lists an incorrect codomain. Option D mistakenly lists the domain as the range.

mcqs.question: Which of the following mapping diagrams correctly represents a function from X = {a, b, c} to Y = {1, 2, 3}?
mcqs.explanation: A mapping diagram represents a function when every element of the domain X has exactly one arrow pointing to an element of the codomain Y. Option A satisfies this: each of a, b, c maps to a single, distinct element, so it is a valid function. Option B shows b mapping to two different outputs (2 and 3), violating the definition. Option C leaves c without any image, so the mapping is not defined for every domain element. Option D gives a two‑arrow mapping for a, again breaking the rule of a single output per input.
